title: Nine Posters of Ink
subtitle: 运动与活动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 运动与活动（社会服务与人际沟通·公益与宣传）
meta: 主题语境：运动与活动（社会服务与人际沟通·公益与宣传）　|　核心词汇：campaign　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 campaign 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my mother was sent to run ① a campaign she could not name, and she said the naming was the whole of the lesson. The ② campaign, meaning the posters and not the cause, was nine weeks long and was run by whoever came last; a campaign, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ campaign in that town had the same slogan, and the ④ campaign at the end, meaning the one the secretary kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever run properly. A campaign, my grandmother said, is nine parts ink and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the ink is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ campaign was the whole of the cause, meaning the cause it served and not the posters. The ⑥ campaign, meaning the cause and not any of that, is the only thing in a street that everybody signs and nobody questions; a campaign, he said, is either something you run or the only word that means both posters and a cause. She said the cause is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ campaign had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the slogan. The ⑧ campaign of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine weeks and eleven years of running; a campaign, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ campaign I remember is the one at the end, which was won in 1979 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ campaign, my grandmother said in 1984, is the only thing that improves by being won; every campaign, she said, is a cause that has agreed to look like posters. She said the cause was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 运动；活动（为某一目标而开展）
B. n. 运动（指那些海报、活动本身，与事业相对）
C. 固定搭配：run a campaign 开展／组织一场运动
D. n. 运动（指镇上每一场）
E. n. 运动（指末尾那一场）
F. n. 运动（抽象：它服务的那项事业）
G. n. 那项事业（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a campaign she could not name
The campaign, meaning the posters and not the cause
campaign was the whole of the cause
the campaign had become a photograph in a report
The campaign of the whole thing
A campaign, my grandmother said in 1984

answers.why: run a campaign 意为“开展／组织一场运动”，1959 年母亲被派去组织一场她说不出名字的运动。
campaign 意为“运动”，指那些海报、活动本身而不是事业，持续九周，由最后走的人组织。
campaign 指镇上每一场运动，每一场都是同样的口号。
campaign 指末尾那一场（干事管的一场），是唯一有人认真组织的。
campaign 意为“运动”，抽象指它服务的那项事业，父亲说 campaign 就是那项事业的全部。
campaign 为抽象用法，指那项事业本身，是街上人人都签名、却没人质疑的东西。
campaign 意为“运动、活动”，到 1974 年这场 campaign 成了报告里的一张照片。
campaign 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九周和十一年的组织。
campaign 意为“运动”，我记得的是末尾那一场，1979 年取胜，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
campaign 为抽象总称，祖母说一场运动是唯一会因为赢得胜利而变好的东西。
